videos.script: Lesson seven called one provider. This lesson calls two more, Google and Cohere, with their own Python libraries. {{sdks}} The calls look alike. Text goes in, a list of numbers comes back. {{shape}} The differences are where the interest is. Both providers ask you a question that OpenAI does not. What is this text for? {{question}} A customer's question and the article that answers it are different kinds of text. One is short and asks. The other is long and explains. {{sides}} Models trained for search learn that difference. So you tell them which side each text is on, a query or a document. {{labels}} The lab's server accepts those labels and ignores them, because its two models are symmetric. You will see that for yourself. {{same}} Cohere can also hand back each vector in smaller forms. Small integers, or one bit per number. {{bits}} You will measure what that costs on the help centre's twenty-four questions. {{measure}} Then you will put three providers side by side, from one price sheet, and see what a million documents would cost with each. {{table}}
